title: Tutoring Large Language Models to be Domain-adaptive, Precise, and Safe
benchmark_measurement: The paper introduces the 'Cultural Harm Evaluation Dataset' which measures biases and cultural harm across 12 sensitive topics, including religious sensitivities and local taboos, in multi-turn conversations.
findings: The paper finds that models can be fine-tuned to significantly reduce culturally harmful outputs (which includes religious insensitivity) by using preference optimization (ORPO) on culturally specific datasets. For example, Mistral-7B's cultural harm rate was reduced from 71.96% to 3.07%. Additionally, a lightweight parameter steering method ('Soteria') can reduce policy violations across multiple languages without full retraining.
